rationale: Java reaches both ratios exactly, so the floor is the measurement rather than a margin below it; only `calls` keeps a hair of slack against a grammar update introducing a call node type the walker has not seen. The files were chosen for the shapes that were broken before ATL-096, and the pre-fix walker scores 0.381 / 0.370 on this same directory: anonymous inner classes in a field initializer (ArrayTypeAdapter, TypeAdapters), in an interface constant (ReflectionAccessFilter), as a call argument and a return value (RuntimeTypeAdapterFactory), four instantiations of the same base inside one method (UnsafeAllocator, which is what forces the `$Base$2` suffix), an enum whose constants carry bodies and whose members follow them in `enum_body_declarations` (FieldNamingPolicy), and local classes declared inside method bodies (ReadersWritersTest). 565 lambdas across the full gson checkout get no entity by design (ADR-0031) and are excluded from `named_funcs`; their calls are attributed to the enclosing method, which is why `calls` is 1.0 despite them. On the full 264-file checkout the walker is also 1.000 / 1.000 — every method_invocation and object_creation_expression node in gson becomes a CALLS relationship, verified file by file with no file over- or under-emitting.
retrievability_rationale: Searchable content bytes (docstring + source + signature, at the production max_source_chars of 2000) over file bytes. Deliberately NOT embed text: that carries a breadcrumb header which grows with entity count, so a walker emitting more nodes would raise the ratio without making one more byte findable. Measured 2026-08-30. Above 1.0 because a class's source contains its methods' -- the ratio is a floor, not a fraction. Javadoc is attached where it exists.
